basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 20.' and it opens 'Vers. 20. Aser, pinguis panis ejus. Haec verba ad fertilitatem possessionis juxta'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 20. Aser, pinguis panis ejus. Haec verba ad fertilitatem possessionis juxta litteram pertinent. Allegorice vero Aser, qui beatus vel pinguis panis interpretatur, eumdem Christum designat, cujus panis pinguis est, id est corpus ejus, quo ad aeternam vitam reficimur, sicut ipse dixit: Ego sum panis vivus, | qui de coelo descendi, et do vitam huic mundo (Joan. VI, 35). Ipse praebet delicias regibus, id est sanctis, qui motus corporis sui bene regere noverunt. His praebet delicias, id est suavitatem verbi, sive etiam se ipsum, quia Aser deliciae interpretatur.
